lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: creating linear, quadratic, rational, and exponential equations in one variable
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: creating linear, quadratic, rational, and exponential equations in one variable

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: A costs $4, B costs $7, budget $50. Write the constraint.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A tank holds 95 litres and is filling at 5 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 170 litres?
A model gives the number of buses needed as 4.3. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: The model must be wrong, because the answer is not a whole number.
Report 4.3, because the model is exact.
Round up to 5; a fractional bus is not viable and rounding down leaves people behind.
Round down to 4, because 4.3 is closer to 4.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $20 call-out fee plus $4 per hour. A job cost $40 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
The formula A = 5bh − 7 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $10 each and item B costs $24 each. You may spend at most $190 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 30 litres and is filling at 5 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 110 litres?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A model gives a required side length of −6 metres. How should this solution be interpreted?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $290 call-out fee plus $13 per hour. A job cost $433 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
